page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is a shared-resource virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a moderate capability profile. The shared CPU allocation results in a stress-ng single-core performance score of 780.79, which falls into the bottom 10%, and a multi-core score of 3123.05, placing it in the bottom 25%. However, Geekbench testing shows average tier results, with a single-core score of 1409.0 and a multi-core score of 5074.0. Memory bandwidth performance is mixed, showing an average read-only speed of 411.67 GB/sec for small cached blocks, but dropping to a weak 36.0 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks. Passmark memory testing ranks in the bottom 10% with a score of 1246.97.

From a workload perspective, this server is configured for budget-conscious, non-intensive applications. It achieves average performance in software compilation and text processing, but exhibits weaknesses in database operations and Redis SET operations. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, development environments, and basic utility tasks where high CPU consistency and local storage are not critical.
